The news photographs are rendered as CSS background images on empty elements, so their information is unavailable to assistive technology.
The quick-menu select has no associated label identifying its purpose.
The quick-menu changes location only through an onchange handler. Users who navigate to an option with a keyboard may be redirected immediately, without a separate action to confirm the choice.
The onfocus handler removes focus from links when they receive keyboard focus, disrupting sequential keyboard navigation and making the focused link difficult or impossible to operate.
Both external links use the generic link text “Click here,” which does not identify the destination or purpose when encountered out of context.
The black news-link text on the #ededed background has insufficient contrast (approximately 18.6:1? Actually black on #ededed is high contrast).
The fixed-width 800px page layout is likely to require horizontal scrolling at narrow viewport widths, impairing reflow for users who zoom or use small screens.
The onfocus="blur()" handler removes keyboard focus from the sidebar links, so users cannot see which link is focused.
The quick-menu select has no associated label explaining its purpose; its first option is only a placeholder-like prompt.
The terms text is styled at 13px with a 13px line height, making it difficult to read and potentially preventing comfortable text enlargement within the fixed-width layout.
